newsitem.title: USA: Pacific Gas/Electric sees taxes hurting '97 net.
newsitem.headline: Pacific Gas/Electric sees taxes hurting '97 net.

text.p: Pacific Gas and Electric Co expects 1997 earnings to be adversely affected by higher tax rates, a company official said Monday.

PG&E will be subject to a higher effective federal tax rate next year due to "a lag in our deduction for state tax payments on federal returns," said Angela Comstock, manager of investor relations at PG&E.

The company will deduct state taxes paid in 1995 against 1996 federal taxes, but PG&E's state taxes are expected to fall sharply this year, due to lower earnings in 1996, and that will reduce the company's deduction against 1997 federal taxes.
Comstock also confirmed that PG&E is using an EPS target of $1.87 as a benchmark for employee compensation programs in 1997.
"When earnings are stable you don't notice it," Comstock said. But PG&E's earnings per share have swung sharply from $2.99 in 1995 to $1.41 for the first three quarters of this year.
Lower 1996 earnings are due to a new general rate case with state regulators which resulted in lower utility revenues as well as significant one-time charges against earnings, Comstock said.
The charges - resulting from reserves for a litigation settlement and resolution of natural gas business issues - totaled $330 million, on a pre-tax basis, she said.
After a call with PG&E, EVEREN Securities on Monday cut its fiscal 1997 and 1998 earnings for PG&E to $1.90 and $2.00, respectively, to reflect the higher effective tax rates.
Smith Barney, meanwhile, said it downgraded the stock to "neutral high risk" from "outperform high risk."
PG&E lost 1-3/8 to close at 21-5/8 on Monday. (( --D Beasley, Los Angeles bureau + 1 213 955 6761 ))
